address: 2855 Stevens Creek Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95050
w: The Bay Area's first outpost of the world-famous Taiwanese chain, inside Westfield Valley Fair; the hand-folded xiao long bao (pork and pork-crab) are the benchmark for soup dumplings and draw hours-long waits. Open (verified July 2026).

Cupertino's standard-bearer for Taiwanese juancun (military-village) cooking; the beef tendon noodle soup, with many bite-size chunks of beef in a rich but not oily broth, is called one of the best versions in the South Bay. Open (verified July 2026).

address: 587 E El Camino Real, Sunnyvale, CA 94087
w: A boba-and-bento shop (originally Oakland) whose house-special GPIE is a crunchy, well-seasoned ji pai, the oversized fried-chicken cutlet of Taiwanese night markets; the kitchen also runs pop-ups of Taiwanese breakfast fan tuan and dan bing. Open.
A small boba-and-bento shop turning out classic Taiwanese flavors in takeout-friendly rice plates, including a homey lu rou fan (braised pork over rice). Open.
A Taiwanese restaurant-pub built for sharing bar bites over a Taiwan Beer; the standout is san bei ji, three-cup chicken braised with soy, rice wine, sesame oil and basil. Open.
A Cupertino specialist in Taiwanese congee, the soupy rice porridge eaten with a spread of small braised and pickled side dishes. Open.

address: 795 E El Camino Real, Sunnyvale, CA 94087
w: Brews high-quality loose leaf imported from Taiwan and remixes it with bold flavors; the signature torched brûlée milk tea with house-made boba is the draw. Open (verified Aug 2026).
A long-running Cupertino boba spot near Apple Park known for its Okinawa (brown-sugar) milk tea and hot taro milk tea. Open.
